headline: Welcome Back. The Grades Are In.
lede: Two hundred and twenty-four picks, $2,790 spent, seventy-two players gone for a dollar. Every roster here is ranked on one thing: what its eight scoring positions are actually worth once replacement-level dollars come off. That math says the worst franchise in league history drafted one of the two best starting lineups in the room, that the defending champion left $47 of offense on his own bench, and that two of the best drafts belong to men who joined this league in March. Fourteen grades and every price below.
home_headline: Football Is Back And So Are The Receipts
home_lede: Fifteen seasons in, fourteen managers, two new faces and $2,790 set on fire in a single night. The rosters are locked, every dollar is audited, and Week 1 kicks off Sunday. Draft grades, the biggest steal of the night, and preseason power rankings built on what each starting lineup is actually worth are one click away. Nobody is going to agree with any of it. Welcome back.

The spreadsheet loves him more than your eyes will. Lamb and Jefferson for $103, two flex spots to absorb them, and an entire backfield that cost thirty-four dollars.
Zero replacement-level starters and the cheapest man in his lineup cost six dollars. The most boring eight in the draft and one of the two best.
Seven starters between $17 and $35 and nobody who can end his season alone. He also paid the second, fourth and eighth biggest raises of the night to get there.
Sixty percent of the budget on the biggest raise of the draft and the third biggest. Then he built the only bench in the league that is worth anything.
A hundred and eleven dollars on Nacua and Achane and then he kept buying. Highest ceiling in the bottom half, thinnest margin for a hamstring.
Chase and McCaffrey is the best pair anybody owns. Two of the other six starting spots are already filled at replacement price.
Barkley, Jeanty and Nico all came in under last year's price, and then $183 of the $200 made the lineup and two dollars made nothing at all.
Four real starters and then sixteen dollars of excellent players stacked behind them. Move that money one slot forward and he is top five.
Josh Jacobs at $8 was the theft of the night. He then bought eleven players deserving of a roster spot in a league that starts eight.

awards.label: The Theft
awards.note: Josh Jacobs at $8. This exact room paid $43 for him last September. He came off the board fifth and fourteen people watched it happen with their hands in their pockets.

awards.label: The Record
awards.note: $73 for Jahmyr Gibbs, the most expensive player in fifteen years of this league, bought about ninety seconds after the auction opened. The old record was $70 and that team finished sixth.

awards.label: Cleanest Lineup
awards.note: $190 on the field, zero starting spots filled at replacement price. Only one other manager got both of those right and he has been in this league since 2012.

awards.label: The Quarterback Hoard
awards.note: Three quarterbacks, $22, one starting slot. Then a second kicker for a second kicker slot that does not exist. That is $24 spent on positions that were already full.

awards.label: Money In The Wrong Place
awards.note: Sixteen dollars of genuinely good players stacked on his bench, including a $3 Patrick Mahomes who cannot score a point in a one-quarterback league unless Justin Herbert gets hurt.

awards.label: The Bravest Twenty-One Dollars
awards.note: Parker Washington cost $21. Travis Kelce cost $6. DK Metcalf cost $19. No further questions.

awards.label: Highest Floor
awards.note: The cheapest player in his starting lineup cost six dollars. Nobody else can say that. It is the least exciting sentence in this column and it wins a lot of weeks.

awards.label: The Bargain Bin
awards.note: Eight players at a dollar, including Alvin Kamara ($29 last year), T.J. Hockenson ($8) and Keenan Allen. If three of them hit, this whole ranking looks stupid by Halloween.

A dad.headline: Four kings and a fistful of ones
body: A hundred and ninety of his two hundred dollars is standing in the starting lineup, and after the replacement-level dollars are stripped out he is tied for the most starting value in the draft. Amon-Ra St. Brown $60, Kenneth Walker III $43, Brock Bowers $39, Ladd McConkey $28. Then the roster falls off a cliff so cleanly you could film a car commercial on it.

Bowers at $39 is the smartest buy of the night and the easiest one to laugh at. Twenty-four tight ends changed hands at an average of $7.80. He paid five times the market and now owns a weekly advantage at a mandatory slot while thirteen other people roll a die there every Sunday. Paying up at the position nobody wants to pay up at is how a league gets won quietly.

He also spent $1 on Kyler Murray to be his starting quarterback, which in a league that hands out four points for a passing touchdown is not the crime it looks like. The actual exposure is Xavier Worthy at $4 in a flex spot and Chuba Hubbard at $10 as the second back. If St. Brown or Walker misses a month there is nothing behind them but the sound of ones rattling in a cup.
A dad.best: Brock Bowers, $39. The tight end market cleared at $7.80 and he bought a weekly edge with it.
A dad.worst: Kenneth Walker III, $43. Eighteen dollars more than this room paid for the same man last year.

Leo the Cleo.headline: The math has bad news for everybody
body: Sit down for this one. The worst franchise in the history of this league, 33-78 across six seasons with zero playoff appearances, walked out of that room tied for the most starting value in the draft. A hundred and ninety dollars in eight starters, and after replacement is stripped out, nobody has more. Jahmyr Gibbs $73, Kyren Williams $32, Josh Allen $29, Malik Nabers $29, Tony Pollard $18. That is a genuinely frightening front five.

The $73 on Gibbs is the most expensive player in fifteen years of this league, bought roughly ninety seconds after the auction opened, and everybody in that room enjoyed watching him pay it. The previous record was $70 and that team finished sixth. What the laughing missed is that he then bought three more real starters instead of stopping, which is the part nobody expected.

The catch is enormous and it is the reason this is an A- and not an A. Three of his eight starting spots are filled at replacement price: Jakobi Meyers at $4, Jayden Reed at $4, and a $1 tight end. Every other contender has one of those or none. When Gibbs plays, this team beats anybody. When Gibbs sits, three of eight slots are already scoring nothing and a fourth just joined them. The highest ceiling in the league and, by a distance, the lowest floor.
Leo the Cleo.best: Cooper Kupp, $2. He cost $11 here last year.
Leo the Cleo.worst: A one-dollar tight end and a four-dollar WR2. The top five is a contender. The bottom three is a bye week.

Fwamming Gwaggon.headline: The new guy read the room
body: Second name called all night, $69 for Bijan Robinson, and then he never blinked again. A.J. Brown $45, David Montgomery $23, Colston Loveland $22, Jaylen Warren $13, Brian Thomas Jr. $10. He is the only manager in the entire league who got a hundred and ninety dollars into his starting lineup without a single replacement-level body in it. Not one slot filled by a guy anybody could have had for pocket change.

The back half is where it was won. Brian Thomas Jr. cost $10. This exact room paid $50 for him last September. Courtland Sutton cost $5 after going for $27. Two of the four biggest discounts of the night, both his, both bought while eleven other people were still arguing about running backs like it was 2019.

The one wobble is Loveland at $22, a $3 tight end last year in a market that cleared at $7.80. Pay that and he has to be the position, not a guy at the position. Twelve men have been in this league for over a decade and the cleanest draft in the room belongs to somebody who joined in March. The rest of the league should find that considerably more upsetting than they currently do.
Fwamming Gwaggon.best: Brian Thomas Jr., $10. The same fourteen people paid $50 for him twelve months ago.
Fwamming Gwaggon.worst: Colston Loveland, $22. Three times what the tight end market cleared at.

Kim Jong Nate.headline: Two Ferraris and a rented bus
body: CeeDee Lamb $52 and Justin Jefferson $51, both cheaper than last year, and Emeka Egbuka at $25 behind them. On the arithmetic this is a top-four starting lineup, because two flex slots mean a receiver-heavy roster still gets all that money on the field. The eye test and the spreadsheet disagree about this team more than any other and it is worth understanding why.

The entire running back room cost thirty-four dollars. Quinshon Judkins $23, Jacory Croskey-Merritt $9, Kaleb Johnson $1, Sean Tucker $1. That is less than he paid for Justin Jefferson on his own, spread across the position that touches the ball on every snap of every drive. Two starting running back slots get filled by a $23 rookie and a $9 flier, and if either one is not the guy, the flexes stop being a luxury and start being a patch.

Zachariah Branch at $1 is already sitting in a flex spot, which is one slot scoring nothing before the season starts. The ceiling is real, the receivers are the best in the league, and the whole thing rests on a backfield he assembled out of whatever was still moving at nine o'clock.
Kim Jong Nate.best: Jayden Daniels, $10. Half of last year's price for the same quarterback.
Kim Jong Nate.worst: The backfield, $34 total. Four running backs for two thirds of what one CeeDee Lamb cost.

Mac Daddy.headline: The most boring lineup in the draft, and it works
body: Nobody built a cleaner eight. Jonathan Taylor $62, DeVonta Smith $34, Tee Higgins $25, Garrett Wilson $23, Lamar Jackson $21, Rico Dowdle $13, and the cheapest man in his starting lineup cost six dollars. Zero replacement-level starters, a hundred and ninety dollars on the field, and not one slot where you look at the name and wince. In a fourteen-team league that plays two flexes, that matters more than anybody wants to admit in September.

George Kittle at $6 after going $22 last year is the best tight end value of the draft, and $62 for Jonathan Taylor is eighteen dollars of certainty tax on a $44 player from a year ago. Fine. He finished fourth last season with considerably less than this and he did it by never having a hole to plug.

Lamar Jackson at $21 is the one indulgence: the second most expensive quarterback in a league that pays four points for a passing touchdown, in a room where two starters changed hands for ten dollars combined. That is not acquiring a player, that is buying a boat and then telling everyone how much you use it. Behind Dowdle the backfield thins out fast, which is the difference between this and a top-two grade.
Mac Daddy.best: George Kittle, $6. Sixteen dollars cheaper than last year at the position nobody solved.
Mac Daddy.worst: Lamar Jackson, $21. One quarterback slot, four-point passing touchdowns, twenty-one dollars.

Miley 💨LEO 5K Speedo Fan Club.headline: Seven guys who might all be good
body: The flattest competitive roster in the draft and, it turns out, one of the most efficient. Rashee Rice $35, Javonte Williams $33, Trey McBride $30, Travis Etienne $28, Tetairoa McMillan $22, Cam Skattebo $21, Rome Odunze $17. A hundred and eighty-nine dollars on the field, no replacement-level starters anywhere, and nobody who can end the season by pulling up short on a Sunday. Coming off the Sacco, that is exactly the right way to rebuild.

The bill for all that flatness is enormous. Rice went $6 to $35. Javonte went $8 to $33. Etienne went $9 to $28. Those are the second, fourth and eighth biggest raises of the entire night, all sitting on one roster, which means he is not buying value, he is buying last September's breakouts at this September's asking price. Everybody in this room does that every year and every year it is somebody else's turn to be surprised.

Travis Hunter at $1 after costing $16 twelve months ago is the kind of pickup that quietly wins a flex spot in October. The floor here is dramatically higher than last season's catastrophe. The ceiling is capped by the fact that he bought seven very good number twos and never once bought a number one.
Miley 💨LEO 5K Speedo Fan Club.best: Travis Hunter, $1. He cost $16 in this room last September.
Miley 💨LEO 5K Speedo Fan Club.worst: Rashee Rice, $35. Up from $6, and nobody else was within twenty dollars of that bid.

Bend The Knee 🐲🔥.headline: Sixty percent of the money, two names, no holes
body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba at $63 is the single biggest raise of the draft, plus $33 on what this room paid a year ago, and James Cook III at $56 is the third biggest at plus $25. Together they ate $119 of $200. He did not find value on either one. He set the market on both and then had eighty-one dollars to build the rest of a football team.

What that eighty-one bought is a museum of other people's regrets, and it is the reason this grade is higher than it looks like it should be. Alvin Kamara at $1 after $29. T.J. Hockenson at $1 after $8. Travis Kelce at $6 after $14. Keenan Allen at $1. He is one of only four teams with no replacement-level starter, and the only team in the league whose bench is worth anything at all once replacement dollars come off.

And then there is Parker Washington at $21, more than he paid for DK Metcalf and three and a half times what he paid for Travis Kelce, on a player the rest of the room had priced at approximately nothing. One playoff appearance in nine seasons says the careful approach was not working. This is emphatically not the careful approach.
Bend The Knee 🐲🔥.best: Alvin Kamara, $1. Twenty-nine dollars last year. One dollar tonight. Somebody had to.
Bend The Knee 🐲🔥.worst: Parker Washington, $21. Three and a half Travis Kelces.

Poop Squad 💩.headline: A hundred and eleven dollars of hamstring
body: Puka Nacua $63 and De'Von Achane $48. That is $111, fifty-six percent of the budget, on two men whose entire value proposition is remaining structurally intact for four months. When they are upright this team is terrifying. The plan is not complicated and it does not need to be, but it does need a physiotherapist on retainer.

What holds the grade up is that he kept buying after the fireworks. Davante Adams $24, Rhamondre Stevenson $19, MarShawn Lloyd $17, Sam LaPorta at $7 after going $15 last year. A hundred and eighty-nine dollars reached the starting lineup, seventh most in the league. Coming off 7-21 and thirteenth place, this is the first roster he has owned in years with a reason to open the app on Sunday.

Jordan Addison at $4 is already sitting in a flex spot doing nothing, the quarterback plan is Jaxson Dart at $7, and $17 for MarShawn Lloyd is a starter's price for a man who has never held the job. Aggressive was the correct posture from where he finished. This is aggressive.
Poop Squad 💩.best: Sam LaPorta, $7. Eight dollars cheaper than last year for the same tight end.
Poop Squad 💩.worst: MarShawn Lloyd, $17. Seventeen dollars is a lot to pay for a rumor.

Good Will Hunting.headline: The best two players and then a cliff
body: Ja'Marr Chase $63 and Christian McCaffrey $59 is the strongest pair anybody walked out with, and $122 to own it. Seventy-two percent of his money sits in three players, the most concentrated roster in the league. When it works it is unbeatable and when either man misses a month it looks exactly like 2025, where the five biggest buys in this room finished sixth, fourteenth, 8-20, fourth, and in the Sacco Bowl.

Then Jadarian Price at $22, a rookie running back who cost precisely the same as Jalen Hurts, Joe Burrow and Patrick Mahomes combined. Read that again. Three starting quarterbacks, or one man who has not yet been handed a jersey number he gets to keep. Terry McLaurin at $21 after going $30 is genuinely sharp work and Joe Burrow at $11 is a fine answer at the position.

Two of his eight starting spots are already replacement level, Dalton Kincaid at $3 and KC Concepcion at $4, and only Leo the Cleo is carrying more dead weight in a starting lineup. This is a team that wins six weeks by forty and loses six weeks by forty. In a fourteen-team league with six playoff spots, that is a coin flip in a very expensive coat.
Good Will Hunting.best: Terry McLaurin, $21. Nine dollars off last year for the same production.
Good Will Hunting.worst: Jadarian Price, $22. The exact price of Hurts, Burrow and Mahomes stacked on top of each other.

ShakeNBake.headline: Three studs, two dollars, still no ring
body: Saquon Barkley $52, Ashton Jeanty $43, Nico Collins $43, and all three came in under what this room paid for them last year, which is the correct way to be top-heavy: buy the expensive names when the market has gone quiet rather than when it is screaming. That is the good half.

The bad half is that only $183 of the $200 ever reached the starting lineup, seven dollars below the field, because the money after the big three went into Carnell Tate at $13 and Jonathon Brooks at $10, two dart throws being asked to hold down a flex on a contender. Isaiah Likely at $3 is a starting tight end who scores nothing. And two dollars went entirely unspent, which in an auction is not thrift, it is litter.

Fifteen seasons, two runner-up finishes, zero rings, and the roster shape that produced both near misses is sitting right here again: elite at the top, soft in the middle, and a season that turns on whether the third receiver hits. The man who built this website ranked himself tenth on it, which is either integrity or a very long con.
ShakeNBake.best: Mike Evans, $12. He cost $28 in this room a year ago.
ShakeNBake.worst: Two dollars, unspent, plus a three-dollar tight end in a starting slot.

The Asshouse Always Wins.headline: He bought a beautiful bench
body: Derrick Henry $45, Drake London $45, Chris Olave $32, Breece Hall $29. Four real starters and a genuinely composed first draft from somebody who joined this league eight months ago. Nobody is going to enjoy playing him in October. The problem is what happened with the last forty dollars.

Only $180 reached the starting lineup, eleventh in the league, because sixteen dollars went into Patrick Mahomes at $3, Mark Andrews at $4, Khalil Shakir at $3, Deebo Samuel at $3 and Tank Bigsby at $3. Every one of those is a fine player at a fair price and every one of those is worth exactly nothing to a lineup, because they are all sitting behind somebody. Mahomes at $3 got a lot of admiring noise on draft night and he is a backup quarterback in a league with one quarterback slot. He cannot score a point unless Justin Herbert gets hurt.

That is the whole gap between eleventh and fourth: not the players he bought, but where he put them. Sixteen dollars moved from the bench into a real flex and this is a top-five team. Rookie mistake, extremely fixable, and he still drafted better than four men who have been doing this since 2011.
The Asshouse Always Wins.best: Chris Olave and Breece Hall for $61 combined. Two starters for the price of one of Leo's.
The Asshouse Always Wins.worst: Sixteen dollars of very good bench. A backup quarterback in a one-quarterback league cannot score.

The Injured Reserved.headline: The best shopping, the wrong basket
body: Josh Jacobs at $8 is the buy of the draft and it is not close. This room paid $43 for him last September. He came off the board fifth, before anybody had settled into their chair, and fourteen people sat on their hands and let it happen. Nobody bid. Somewhere around November that price is going to look like a felony.

And then the same instinct that found Jacobs kept going long after it should have stopped. Omarion Hampton $47, Zay Flowers $34, Bhayshul Tuten $26, Jaylen Waddle $24, Quentin Johnston $14, Tucker Kraft $13, Chris Godwin $10, Rachaad White $5, Romeo Doubs $5. He bought eleven players who deserve a roster spot in a league that starts eight of them. Only $171 got into the starting lineup, twelfth in the league, and $25 is parked behind it waiting for somebody to get hurt.

Depth wins leagues in November and it does not win them in September, and this is a metric that only counts what starts. He went 21-7 last year and finished fifth, so he knows precisely what he is doing, but the same money arranged differently is a top-five roster instead of a twelfth-place one. Also no kicker and no defense, which costs one waiver claim and nothing else.
The Injured Reserved.best: Josh Jacobs, $8. He cost $43 in this room last year and not one person raised a hand.
The Injured Reserved.worst: Twenty-five dollars of bench. The best value board in the draft, pointed at the wrong slots.

FreeGucci.headline: He turned two hundred dollars into a smoothie
body: Sixteen players, exactly one of them cost a dollar, and not one of them cost more than $44. Chase Brown $44, George Pickens $37, DJ Moore $23, Drake Maye $15, Alec Pierce $14, Michael Pittman $13, Jordan Mason $13, Blake Corum $10. Every price on this roster is a middling price. There is no star to build around and no bargain to feel clever about. He took $200 and blended it until it was completely smooth.

Only $162 of it ever reached a starting lineup, thirteenth of fourteen, with $31 sitting on the bench and five dollars that never left his pocket at all. Spreading money evenly is a genuine strategy in a year when the middle of the board is underpriced. This year the middle of the board was the single most expensive part of it, and he bought all of it.

Three championships says he understands something about this league the rest of us do not. This roster says whatever it is, it did not survive contact with a thirty-seven dollar bid on George Pickens. He owns sixteen players and not one of them is going to be the reason he wins a week.
FreeGucci.best: Zach Charbonnet, $5. Six dollars off last year and a genuine handcuff.
FreeGucci.worst: Alec Pierce, $14. He cost one dollar in this exact room in September.

Hail Mary.headline: Forty-seven dollars of offense on the bench
body: A hundred and fifty dollars of the champion's two hundred reached his starting lineup. That is dead last in the league by twelve dollars and thirty-two below the field. Forty-seven dollars of real offense is sitting behind it, three and a half times what anybody else benched, and it is not depth, it is a filing error. His biggest purchase of the entire night was Jameson Williams at $28.

Some of that is the quarterbacks. He spent $22 on three of them in a league with one quarterback slot and four points for a passing touchdown, so he can start one and the other two are there for emotional support, while Patrick Mahomes went for three dollars to somebody else. Then he bought a second kicker to keep them company. That is $24 of a $200 budget on two roster slots that were already full.

In 2025 he won this thing by refusing to buy anything expensive, and this site called his draft board the most boring document the league had ever produced. He seems to have filed that as a compliment rather than as a description of a market that happened to be cheap that year. Flat works when the middle is underpriced. Tonight the middle was where all the money went, and the commissioner showed up with three quarterbacks and a spare kicker.
Hail Mary.best: TreVeyon Henderson, $13. Fifteen dollars off last year's price.
Hail Mary.worst: The second, third and fourth quarterback. There is one quarterback slot and it was full by eight o'clock.
